examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Compute attribute closure by repeatedly adding right sides whose left sides are already present. A candidate key is a minimal full closure; attributes never on any nontrivial RHS must appear in every key. Apply Armstrong rules to whole sets: XY→Z does not generally imply X→Z or Y→Z.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
R(A,B,C,D) has A→B, B→C, AC→D. How many attributes are in A+?

**Answer: 4.** Start {A}; A→B adds B, B→C adds C, then AC→D adds D. Closure is {A,B,C,D}, of size four. A alone is a candidate key.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Dependency satisfaction is a schema-wide constraint, not a fact proved by one small table instance unless that instance is explicitly the entire semantics.

A dependency observed in current rows is not proof it must hold in every valid database state.
